evals.prompt: Plan only: staff need to download completed request data as CSV for weekly reconciliation. We have two developer days, an existing authenticated request list, and no background-job service. Shape the feature; scheduled exports are optional, not required.
evals.expected_output: A bounded approach and useful manual-export slice, with risks and exclusions.
assertions: Preserves CSV reconciliation value and two-day investment boundary.
Uses an end-to-end manual download candidate rather than presenting only a table or screen.
Makes scheduled export exclusion or tradeoff explicit.
Does not invent a delivery guarantee or implement.

evals.prompt: Shape our feature, no execution: customers must see whether their submitted claim needs more documents. We have one week; claims already have statuses, but document-needed status is sometimes stale. The proposed first slice is just a database migration.
evals.expected_output: A useful customer journey proposal with stale data risk and a bounded first slice.
assertions: Does not call a database migration alone a useful delivered feature.
Connects a customer entry point, status, and next action.
Identifies stale status as a risk to the promised value.
Keeps the one-week budget as a boundary rather than proof.

evals.prompt: Plan only: shape instant international payouts with a half-day budget. The bank integration is unverified and no international payout permission exists. Instant receipt is a hard requirement.
evals.expected_output: A feasibility and authority conflict rather than a deceptively narrowed feature promise.
assertions: Names unverified integration and missing permission.
Does not silently exclude instant receipt while claiming the same feature.
Proposes a bounded next check or decision within planning authority.
Does not execute payouts, buy access, or mandate a six-week cycle.

evals.prompt: Use shape-feature, but our only input is that leadership wants an AI dashboard. We do not know who needs it or what decision it supports. Do not collect new data or implement.
evals.expected_output: An explicit missing problem frame and narrowly useful framing questions, without fabricating feature value.
assertions: Identifies the unknown beneficiary and outcome.
Does not invent a valuable dashboard scope or investment agreement.
Stays within supplied context and read-only authority.

evals.prompt: Plan only: customers need to know whether a submitted document was received. Budget is two days, and processing may take several hours. The current candidate screen says Complete immediately on upload, though processing can later fail. Shape a useful small slice.
evals.expected_output: A bounded receipt and processing journey showing relevant waiting and failure/recovery without claiming immediate completion.
assertions: Distinguishes received from processed.
Includes waiting and consequential failure or next-action behavior for this journey.
Preserves budget as a boundary and avoids inventing every possible state.
Does not implement or promise observed delivery performance.

evals.prompt: Plan only: shape an agent-built CSV export with a one-day investment budget and a Friday deadline. The completion endpoint is a locally checked artifact. One comparable task on model M and harness H took 25 measured minutes including one repair, but this task needs an unverified parser. A hosted endpoint is optional and its account approval may take a day. Forecast only if useful.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes budget, deadline, and uncertain agent forecast using the limited comparison; identifies parser uncertainty and conditional external waiting.
assertions: Uses the actual agent executor and local checked endpoint, with comparison limits and uncertainty.
Does not default to human-team weeks, universal AI compression, or invented precise duration.
Treats optional hosted waiting as conditional rather than unavoidable and accounts for dependencies/coordination where relevant.

evals.prompt: Plan only: give a rough estimate for our human team to add a reconciled CSV download. One developer owns the API; another can connect the UI only after columns are agreed. Our budget is three developer days; completion means reviewed code. We have no comparable timing evidence.
evals.expected_output: An explicitly assumed human-team estimate or range with dependency and coordination uncertainty, separate from the budget.
assertions: Honors the explicit human-team executor rather than replacing it with an agent estimate.
Distinguishes investment budget from forecast and reviewed-code endpoint.
States assumptions and dependent work without inventing observed timings or a delivery guarantee.
